inspiration.source_location: FIND_IN_SET-FIELD.sql: documented SELECT examples and filtering use cases
inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL filter uses FIND_IN_SET to test whether a selected label occurs in a comma-separated value column, while the function also exposes the one-based position of the match.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored report-visibility query. Fixed report rows expose positions for two requested labels and a second ordered query filters reports matching either label; NULL, empty, and nonmatching lists remain in the source data to exercise zero and NULL results. The schema, labels, and reporting purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Reports 10 and 20 match ops; reports 10 and 30 match finance. Report 40 has a NULL label list and report 50 has an empty list, so FIND_IN_SET returns NULL for the NULL list and 0 for the empty or missing membership cases.
determinism_notes: All report IDs, labels, and comma-separated lists are fixed; both result sets are ordered by the unique report ID. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE saved_reports (report_id INT PRIMARY KEY, report_title VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, audience_labels VARCHAR(64) NULL)

INSERT INTO saved_reports VALUES (10, 'Quarterly finance', 'ops,finance'), (20, 'Operations runbook', 'ops,qa'), (30, 'Finance archive', 'finance,legal'), (40, 'Unclassified note', NULL), (50, 'Empty audience', '')

steps.sql: SELECT report_id, FIND_IN_SET('ops', audience_labels) AS ops_position, FIND_IN_SET('finance', audience_labels) AS finance_position FROM saved_reports ORDER BY report_id
SELECT report_id, report_title FROM saved_reports WHERE FIND_IN_SET('ops', audience_labels) > 0 OR FIND_IN_SET('finance', audience_labels) > 0 ORDER BY report_id
